title: A 100Gbaud 4Vppd Distributed Linear Driver with Cross-Folded Transmission Lines and Cross-Coupled Gm Cells for Built-in 5-Tap FFE in 0.13µm SiGe BiCMOS
problem: Linear pluggable optics (LPO) drivers must provide large output swing (high extinction ratio), high gain, and wide bandwidth simultaneously for short-reach fiber optics; conventional distributed amplifiers lack equalization, while transmission-line (TL) based FFE designs cannot achieve both high gain and large swing.
motivation: Linear optical drivers enable low-power, low-latency short-reach optical communication; integrating 5-tap feed-forward equalization eliminates external DSP overhead.
method: A distributed linear driver using cross-folded transmission lines and cross-coupled Gm cells that achieves both high gain and large output swing (4 Vppd). The transmission lines provide dual functionality: (1) passive frequency-response shaping for bandwidth extension, and (2) passive delay-line FFE implementation with 5 programmable taps for equalization.
key_novelty: First demonstration of cross-folded TL-based distributed driver achieving simultaneous high gain (low-loss drive) and large swing (4 Vppd) with integrated 5-tap FFE for LPO at 100 Gbaud.
contributions: Cross-folded transmission-line topology combining high gain and large swing capability
Cross-coupled Gm cells providing efficient gain with reduced parasitics
Integrated 5-tap FFE using TL delay-line approach for pre-equalization of modulator
100 Gbaud operation in 0.13 µm SiGe BiCMOS enabling practical LPO deployment
baselines: TL-based FFE drivers without high gain
limitations: Power consumption, total harmonic distortion, and optical extinction-ratio improvement not specified in abstract.
primary_theme: Integrated 100 Gbaud linear LPO driver with cross-folded TL architecture and built-in 5-tap FFE
